Kholmets Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kholmets, Ukraine

Demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery existed by 1875 per epigraphic data, used at least into the 1910s, with its latest preserved gravestone dated 1906. Jews are believed to have arrived in the late 18th century; population reached 80 by 1880 and 83 by 1910, declining to 58 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period) before rising to 61 by 1930. Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, persecuting Jews and forcing them from their occupations; population reached 75 by 1941, when area Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Some families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered; remaining Kholmets Jews were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
